svg.title: TransUNet 2-D slice adapter and metric boundary
svg.desc: A hand-authored architecture map for the project's TransUNet path. A processed 3-D BraTS case is flattened into 2-D slices, resized into an external R50-ViT-B/16 TransUNet checkout, adapted from four external classes into canonical ET, TC, and WT region logits, and scored with slice metrics. A separate native 3-D lane makes the reconstruction and metric boundary explicit: TransUNet does not reconstruct volumes and its unit-spaced per-slice HD95 is not native 3-D full-volume HD95.

g.text: TransUNet stays 2-D. The metric contract stays honest.
Slice the case explicitly, cross the external R50-ViT boundary deliberately, then return canonical logits without inventing volume inference.
same ET / TC / WT names · different inference unit
the active TransUNet route consumes one 2-D slice batch at a time
isolated checkout, not native project code
fourth kernel = mean of original RGB kernels
logits use log_softmax; probabilities are validated
NEVER GUESS CLASS IDs AS LOGITS
same canonical order; metric protocol still depends on dimensionality
same canonical region names; different sampling unit, inference path, and HD95 meaning
not the TransUNet route; shown to keep comparison fair
explicit positive spacing · active BraTS config = (1.0, 1.0, 1.0)
full-volume evaluator uses case-level aggregation; it never receives slice batches.
Per-slice means and unit-spaced HD95 must not be compared directly with native 3-D per-case scores.
The evaluator intentionally stops here. It does not rebuild [D,H,W] from slice predictions.
FACT ANCHORS transunet.py::TransUNetSliceAdapter · adapt_transunet_output · resize_slice · _baseline_common.py::build_slice_loaders · evaluate_slices
hand-authored · grayscale-safe · embedded styles · no external resources
